result.report:
I'll consolidate these verification results into a concise report.

# Pillar-3 PD/LGD/EAD Backtest — Verification Consolidation

## 1. Overall Verdict
**Numeric extraction is uniformly accurate; the integrity risk is class-labeling, not values.** Across all 8 banks (155 rows), every spot-checked PD/LGD/EAD matches the disclosed EU-CR6 A-IRB subtotal — but **3 banks carry must-fix class-mislabel/fabrication errors** (BNP, ING, Credit Mutuel) that would contaminate the Vasicek calibration for specific classes, plus coverage gaps in 2 banks.

## 2. Must-Fix Findings (ERROR / likely_extraction_error)

| Bank | Class (as labeled) | Vintage(s) | Issue |
|------|-------------------|------------|-------|
| **BNP Paribas** | `sme_corporate` | 2022, 2023, 2024 | Rows are the adjacent **"Corporates – Specialised financing"** subtotal (EAD ~71k, PD ~3.8–4.6%, LGD 14–25%), NOT the true SME book (EAD ~34–42k, PD ~6–7%, LGD 28–30%). Systematic mismatch understates SME PD. **Fix:** relabel to `specialised_financing` or re-extract true SME subtotal. |
| **ING Groep** | `qrre` | 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 (all 4) | Mislabeled. ING discloses **no QRRE A-IRB block** in any year. All 4 rows are actually **"Retail – Secured by immovable property SME"** (PD ~3.8–4.3%, LGD ~16–24%). Feeding a secured-RE-SME book in as unsecured revolving retail (true LGD ~40%+) misrepresents the risk profile. **Fix:** rename `qrre` → `mortgage_sme`. |
| **Credit Mutuel** | `sovereign` | 2024 | **Fabricated row** — byte-for-byte duplicate of the `bank` 2024 row (PD=0.12, LGD=34.00, EAD=30,410). Credit Mutuel has **no IRB sovereign exposure** (central govts permanently on standard approach). **Fix:** drop the row before backtesting. |

Three banks — **Deutsche Bank, Banco Santander, Groupe BPCE** — are fully clean (no must-fix issues).

## 3. WARN-Severity / Documentation Items (benign, but should be noted)

**Coverage gaps (real disclosed data omitted from CSV — uneven walk-forward panel, no bad value entered):**

| Bank | What's missing | Detail |
|------|---------------|--------|
| **UniCredit** | `sovereign` 2021, `other_retail` 2021 | Both disclosed in 2021 report (sovereign EAD 24,824/PD 0.10/LGD 21.48; other_retail EAD 22,912/PD 4.98/LGD 42.84); series silently start one year late. |
| **Société Générale** | large-`corporate` (all years), `bank` (2021–2023), `sovereign` 2022 | Large-corporate (~150–170bn EAD) **never** captured (only Corporate-SME); bank only captured for 2024; sovereign 2022 (~271,679 EAD) dropped because PD/LGD failed to extract from concatenated-text PDF. |
| **ING Groep** | `Retail Other non-SME` (all years) | Genuine separate disclosed class entirely absent; combined with the qrre mislabel, ING's retail decomposition doesn't match disclosed structure. |
| **Credit Mutuel** | `bank` 2023 | F-IRB banks subtotal disclosed (EAD 29,543) but not carried into CSV. |

**Real-world changes that are NOT errors (document so they aren't re-flagged):**
- **Deutsche Bank** — Institutions PD spikes (9.32% in 2021, 12.40% in 2022) are genuine EAD-weighted subtotals inflated by a 100%-default band, resolving to 0.19% by 2024; sovereign LGD step-up ~52%→~66% (2023) is a disclosed recalibration.
- **Banco Santander** — bank EAD 38,552→2,748 and corporate 152,167→43,719 (2022→2023) are the documented **AIRB→FIRB rollback** (perimeter shrank), verified across two reports. 2023-report restatement of the 2022 Institutions comparative is a Santander reporting quirk; CSV correctly used each year's as-disclosed current-year figure.
- **BNP / ING** — mortgage/QRRE LGD jumps and the ING sme_corporate EAD near-doubling (26,466→49,548) are all real disclosed moves.
- **BPCE** — high retail PDs (mortgage 14.68%, other_retail 21.55%) are genuine 100%-default-band-inflated subtotals, not errors.

## 4. Spot-Check Coverage

**All 8 banks were spot-checked against source PDFs** (`spotchecked_against_pdf: true` for every bank) — none are CSV-only. Depth varied:

| Depth | Banks |
|-------|-------|
| **Full value-by-value vs source SUB-TOTAL rows** | BNP Paribas (all 21), Groupe BPCE (all 7) |
| **Multi-year matched against multiple report PDFs** | Deutsche Bank (3 doubted values), Banco Santander (2022/2023/2024 reports, cross-report restatement check), UniCredit (2021/2022/2024 PDFs), ING (2021–2024 reports), Société Générale (2021/2022/2024 + 2023 via comparative columns), Credit Mutuel (2023/2024 PDFs) |

---
**Bottom line:** Ship after fixing the 3 class-label/fabrication errors (BNP `sme_corporate`, ING `qrre`, Credit Mutuel `sovereign` 2024). The 4 coverage gaps shorten the panel for affected classes and should be backfilled or explicitly documented as exclusions. All flagged cross-year jumps are confirmed real disclosed changes and require no extraction fix.

perBank.summary: All 28 Deutsche Bank rows (7 classes x 4 vintages 2021-2024) are faithful to the disclosed EU-CR6 A-IRB subtotals. The three values I most doubted were verified directly against the source PDFs and all reconcile exactly: (1) Institutions PD 9.32% in 2021 and 12.40% in 2022 are NOT wrong-row matches but genuine EAD-weighted subtotals inflated by a large 100%-Default PD band (EUR 1,754m of 19,804m in 2021; EUR 2,466m of 20,682m in 2022), which resolves out by 2023 (PD 0.88%) and 2024 (PD 0.19%). The defaulted band carries near-zero LGD (1.12% / 0.37%), so subtotal LGD stays normal. (2) The sovereign LGD step-up from ~52% (2021-22) to ~66% (2023-24) is a real disclosed LGD recalibration -- every PD band on the 2023 page shows LGD ~65-66%. PD/LGD all in range, no PD=0 for non-sovereign, all EAD>0, densities plausible, and cross-year EAD/PD/LGD move smoothly for corporate, mortgage, qrre, other_retail, sme_corporate. No extraction errors or contamination found.

findings.issue: Institutions A-IRB subtotal PD is 12.40%, extraordinarily high for an interbank/institutions class (normally <1%), and PD then collapses to 0.88% (2023) and 0.19% (2024). On its face this looks like a wrong-row (defaulted sub-band) match.
findings.evidence: DB 2022 Pillar 3 p.112, EU CR6 AIRB, Institutions: 'Sub-total 14,832 7,153 39.77 20,682 12.40 0.7 43.74 2.0 3,740 18.08 24 10' -> EAD post-CRM 20,682, PD 12.40%, LGD 43.74%, exactly matching CSV. The 12.40% is a genuine EAD-weighted subtotal pulled up by the '100.00 (Default)' band of EUR 2,466m (~12% of 20,682m) at PD=100%/LGD 0.37%. Faithful extraction of a real disclosed figure.

findings.issue: Institutions A-IRB subtotal PD is 9.32% (again very high for institutions), preceding the 2022 12.40% spike.
findings.evidence: DB 2021 Pillar 3 p.118, EU CR6 AIRB, Institutions: 'Sub-total 14,740 6,339 47.49 19,804 9.32 1.2 40.94 1.7 4,381 22.12 21 7' -> EAD 19,804, PD 9.32%, LGD 40.94%, exact match to CSV. Driven by the '100.00 (Default)' band of EUR 1,754m (~8.9% of 19,804m) at PD=100%/LGD 1.12%. Real disclosed subtotal, not a mis-matched row.

findings.issue: Central-government LGD jumps from ~52% (2021/2022) to ~66% (2023) while PD/EAD stay smooth -- a sizeable level shift that could indicate a wrong-row match or model recalibration.
findings.evidence: DB 2023 Pillar 3 p.104, EU CR6 AIRB, Central governments and central banks: 'Sub-total 120,439 1,609 37.78 128,836 0.24 0.2 66.29 1.3 16,198 12.57 170 43' -> EAD 128,836, PD 0.24%, LGD 66.29%, exact match to CSV. Every individual PD band on the page shows LGD ~65-66% (vs ~50% in 2021/2022), confirming a genuine disclosed upward LGD recalibration on the sovereign book, not an extraction error.

findings.issue: The CSV 'sme_corporate' rows are NOT populated from BNP's 'SME corporates' EU-CR6 subtotal. They are taken from the adjacent 'Corporates - Specialised financing' subtotal on the same corporate page. This is a consistent (systematic) row-mismatch across all three vintages, not a random grab, but it is a misclassification: the true SME book has materially higher PD (~6-7% vs the ~4% used) and different LGD. Using the lower-PD specialised-financing series under the sme_corporate label will bias that Vasicek class's IRB calibration/backtest.
findings.evidence: bnp_2024.pdf p441 Table 39 'Corporates - Specialised financing' SUB-TOTAL = 'SUB-TOTAL 59,281 22,019 56% 71,680 3.78% 25% 3 29,818 42% 1,024 (978)' (EAD 71,680 / PD 3.78% / LGD 25%) -> exactly CSV sme_corporate 2024 (3.78/25/71680). The ACTUAL 'SME corporates' SUB-TOTAL on the same page = 'SUB-TOTAL 29,536 10,593 41% 34,145 7.02% 30% 3 19,799 58% 1,035 (986)' (EAD 34,145 / PD 7.02% / LGD 30%) and is NOT in the CSV. Same pattern in bnp_2023.pdf: p409 specialised-fin SUB-TOTAL 69,038/4.61%/13% = CSV sme_corporate 2023; true SME SUB-TOTAL 39,427/7.24%/28% omitted. p411 (FY2022) specialised-fin SUB-TOTAL 71,400/4.60%/14% = CSV sme_corporate 2022; true SME 41,754/6.16%/28% omitted.

findings.issue: LGD jump 13% -> 25% on the sme_corporate row looked like a possible wrong-row match, but it is a genuine disclosed move within BNP's Specialised-financing book (the series the CSV actually used).
findings.evidence: bnp_2023.pdf p409 specialised-fin SUB-TOTAL '...69,038 4.61% 13% 3...' (LGD 13%); bnp_2024.pdf p441 specialised-fin SUB-TOTAL '...71,680 3.78% 25% 3...' (LGD 25%). Both extracted correctly; the 13->25 LGD shift is in the source.

findings.issue: Mortgage LGD 12% -> 17% jump verified as a real disclosed change, not a mis-match. PD 2.00% in 2022 is genuinely the rounded figure printed in the report (not an extraction artifact).
QRRE LGD drop 52% -> 36% verified as a real disclosed change (correctly extracted), not a flipped/wrong row.
Bank (Institutions) EAD +21% (37,244 -> 45,122) is a genuine disclosed perimeter/exposure change, not a duplicated or mis-matched row. PD/LGD continuity is smooth.

Sovereign (Central bank/central government) low PD (0.08-0.09%) and low LGD (2-3%) are correct disclosed values; EAD declines 452,804 -> 431,674 -> 364,093 smoothly. The note that BNP excludes 2021 (PD rounded to integer in source) is consistent with included years using two-decimal PDs.
Large/'Other' corporate subtotal correctly extracted; PD 2.52->2.73->2.87 and LGD 33->32->37 move smoothly. Correctly distinguished from the specialised-financing and SME sub-portfolios.

perBank.summary: All 21 BNP Paribas rows (7 classes x 2022/2023/2024) were verified value-by-value against the source SUB-TOTAL rows in bnp_2024.pdf (FY2024 + FY2023 comparatives) and bnp_2023.pdf (FY2023 + FY2022 comparatives). Every PD/LGD/EAD number is an accurate transcription of the disclosed EU-CR6 A-IRB subtotal, and the cross-year jumps I initially doubted (mortgage LGD 12->17, qrre LGD 52->36, bank EAD +21%, specialised-fin LGD 13->25) are all REAL disclosed changes, not wrong-row matches. ONE substantive issue: the rows labeled 'sme_corporate' are not BNP's SME corporates subtotal -- they are the adjacent 'Corporates - Specialised financing' subtotal (EAD ~71k, PD ~3.8-4.6%, LGD 14-25%). The genuine SME corporates subtotal (EAD ~34-42k, PD ~6-7%, LGD 28-30%) was omitted. This systematic misclassification understates the SME class PD and would bias the IRB backtest for that Vasicek class. Densities sane throughout. Recommend either relabeling the existing rows to 'specialised_financing'/'project_finance' or re-extracting the true SME subtotal for the sme_corporate class.

findings.issue: Institutions AIRB EAD collapses 38,552 (2022) -> 2,748 (2023), a ~14x drop, with simultaneous LGD drop 38.88% -> 14.34% and PD jump 0.21% -> 0.94%. This triple-move (EAD x14 + LGD flip + PD jump) is exactly the signature of a wrong-row match, so it was the prime suspect.

findings.issue: Cross-report check: the 2023 report's 31.12.2022 COMPARATIVE column for Institutions reads 31,443 / 0.21% / 40.47% -- which equals the CSV's 2021 bank row, NOT its 2022 row (38,552/38.88). Looked like a possible vintage mislabel.

perBank.summary: All 24 Banco Santander rows (6 classes x 2021-2024) verified against the source EU-CR6 AIRB 'Subtotal (exposure class)' rows in santander_2022.pdf, santander_2023.pdf, and santander_2024.pdf. Every checked PD/LGD/EAD value is an exact match to the disclosed subtotals. PD (0.21-13.94%), LGD (10-70%), and EAD (>0) are all in plausible range; densities (RW% printed in source) are reasonable; no PD=0. The two dramatic moves I most doubted are confirmed REAL disclosed changes, not extraction errors: (1) bank/Institutions AIRB EAD 38,552->2,748 with LGD 38.88->14.34 and PD 0.21->0.94 across 2022->2023, and (2) corporate AIRB EAD 152,167->43,719 -- both are the documented 2022->2023 IRB-rollback (AIRB perimeter shrank to FIRB), verified in two independent reports. One nuance: the 2023 report restated the prior-year Institutions comparative to 31,443/40.47% (matching CSV's 2021 value); the CSV correctly used each year's own as-disclosed current-year figure, so this is a Santander reporting quirk, not a CSV error. No contamination or wrong-row matches found. Overall clean.

perBank.summary: Verified all 22 UniCredit AIRB EU-CR6 rows. Opened the 2021, 2022 and 2024 Pillar-3 PDFs and matched every PD/LGD/EAD to the disclosed exposure-class 'Subtotal' rows (Institutions, Corporates-SME, Corporates-Other, QRRE, Central-governments, Retail-Other-non-SME). Every present value is extraction-correct. The three apparent discontinuities (bank LGD 32->22%, SME PD 9.5->6.7%, QRRE PD 5.4->3.7% in 2024) are all genuine disclosed changes confirmed in source, not wrong-row mismatches; densities (RWA/EAD) are plausible and continuous for all classes. The 'header-bleed relabel' note on sovereign is cosmetic only (the row label wraps across PDF lines) and maps to the correct Central-governments subtotal with non-zero PD. No contamination, no implausible values, no PD=0. The only real issues are two completeness gaps: the 2021-12-31 vintages for sovereign (EAD24,824/PD0.10/LGD21.48) and other_retail (EAD22,912/PD4.98/LGD42.84) are disclosed in the 2021 report but are missing from the CSV, so those two series silently start one year late.

perBank.summary: All 19 SocGen values PRESENT in the CSV are confirmed correct against the source Pillar-3 PDFs (socgen_2021/2022/2024; 2023 verified via the comparative columns embedded in socgen_2024.pdf pp.137-140). Every captured PD/LGD/EAD matches an EU-CR6 AIRB 'Subtotal' row exactly, with smooth, plausible cross-year continuity and sensible RWA densities — no wrong-row matches, no LGD flips, no implausible jumps. The flagged sovereign-2021 PD=1.00% / LGD=2.70% (EAD 265,428) is a GENUINE disclosed exposure-weighted level (confirmed verbatim on socgen_2021.pdf p.150), not an extraction error; later years legitimately drop to ~0.10%. The 'DENSITY?' retail rows are clean. No contamination found. The only issues are COVERAGE GAPS, not value errors: (1) the large-Corporate class is disclosed every year (~150-170bn EAD) but NEVER captured (only Corporate-SME is); (2) the bank/Institutions class is disclosed every year but only captured for 2024; (3) sovereign 2022 (EAD ~271,679) is missing because its PD/LGD failed to extract from the concatenated-text 2022 PDF. These produce an uneven panel for the walk-forward backtest and are worth fixing, but no incorrect figure was entered.

findings.issue: The class labeled 'qrre' (Qualifying Revolving Retail) is mislabeled. ING discloses NO QRRE A-IRB block in EU-CR6 in any year (2021-2024). All four 'qrre' rows are in fact ING's 'Retail - Secured by immovable property SME' (mortgage-SME, real-estate-collateralised) class. The numeric values are correctly extracted, but the class IDENTITY is wrong. For an IRB backtest this is contamination: a secured real-estate SME portfolio (LGD ~16-24%, PD ~3.8-4.3%) is being fed in as 'qualifying revolving retail', which in reality is unsecured revolving credit with very different LGD (typically 40%+) and dynamics.

A full scan of 2023 CR6 detail pages (40-55) found NO 'Qualifying revolving' detail block (QRRE detail block present: False).

perBank.summary: All 24 ING numeric values were verified against the source EU-CR6 A-IRB subtotal rows in the 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 ING Additional Pillar III reports and every PD/LGD/EAD matches the disclosed subtotal exactly - the numeric extraction is accurate. The two largest cross-year moves I doubted are real disclosed changes, not wrong-row matches: sme_corporate EAD 26,466->49,548 (2022->2023, Corporates-SME subtotal, corroborated by 2024=47,644) and the secured-RE-SME LGD jump 16.66->23.72 (2021->2022). The serious defect is a CLASS-LABEL contamination, not a value error: the four rows tagged 'qrre' are actually ING's 'Retail - Secured by immovable property SME' (mortgage-SME) class - ING discloses no Qualifying Revolving Retail A-IRB block in any year. Feeding a secured real-estate SME book into an IRB backtest as 'QRRE' misrepresents the risk profile (real QRRE is unsecured, LGD ~40%+). Separately, ING's disclosed 'Retail Other non-SME' class is omitted from the series entirely. Recommend renaming qrre -> mortgage_sme (or secured_re_sme) and either adding the Retail-Other-non-SME class or documenting its exclusion.

findings.issue: The sovereign 2024 row (PD=0.12, LGD=34.00, EAD=30410) is byte-for-byte identical to the bank 2024 row. Credit Mutuel discloses NO IRB sovereign exposure at all: in cm_2024.pdf the F-IRB table (Tableau, p.53/PDF page 52) contains only 'Etablissements (banques)' and 'Entreprises' subtotals, and the page explicitly states 'Les administrations centrales et banques centrales sont durablement en approche standard' (central governments/central banks are permanently on the standard approach; also CR6A on p.54 shows souverains at 100% SA, 0% IRB).
